oracle_provenance.extract_method: simpleFoam laminar steady solve of a 2D plane channel (D=2H=1, Re=100, nu=0.01); U sampled on the centerline y=0 via sampleDict; u_centerline_ratio = Ux(x=1.0)/u_mean, linear-interpolated to the station (solution/solve_inner.py).
oracle_provenance.evals: The clean-rerun evaluator reproduced u_centerline_ratio = 1.2464664 at the declared operating point.

stopping.note: Shipped with endTime 2000 against 1672 measured iterations -- converged, by 20%, on one host. The cap is raised to above twice the measured cost so a slower path to the same criterion still converges rather than silently reporting the cap's answer. The run is unchanged either way: re-measured at endTime 4000 it stops at the same 1672 iterations with the same u_centerline_ratio = 1.2464664, so gt_value does not move (#286).

oracle_provenance.kpi_quality_note: The KPI is sampled in the developing region, before the fully developed plane-Poiseuille limit. The clean-rerun evaluator requires a reproduced OpenFOAM mesh, solution and result artifact.

source.data_source: OpenFOAM ESI v2412 simpleFoam laminar solve sampled on the channel centerline, anchored to the canonical plane-channel entrance-flow problem described in standard viscous-flow texts.
source.physics_note: Re = u_mean*D/nu = 100 (D = 2H = 1, u_mean = 1, nu = 0.01). Hydrodynamic entry length L_e ~ 0.04*Re*D = 4.0; domain length 6.0 leaves >1.5 L_e for full development. KPI station x = 0.01*Re*(2H) = 1.0 sits inside the developing region, so the centerline has only partially accelerated from the uniform inlet (ratio 1.0) toward the fully-developed parabolic value (ratio 1.5).

u_centerline_ratio.description: Channel-centerline (y=0) streamwise velocity U_x at the developing station x = 0.01*Re*(2H) = 1.0, normalised by the mean velocity u_mean (= the uniform inlet velocity). Strictly between 1.0 (uniform inlet) and 1.5 (fully-developed plane Poiseuille).
u_centerline_ratio.pass_tol_source: Flat 5% of |gt_value| — the single band every live track carries (#190, after #188 set it for combustion and battery). The band exists to catch a wrong configuration, not to grade numerical precision, and scoring inside it is binary. Unchanged in value — this case already carried 5%. gt_value is this repository's laminar simpleFoam oracle at the specified station, and the oracle reproduces it; the flow is laminar, so the task leaves no closure form free. The band covers the mesh-resolution and interpolation spread of the developing-region centerline value; gross under-development (too-short domain, too-coarse mesh) and the fully-developed shortcut both land well outside it. An earlier version of this note still called gt_value a placeholder to be calibrated before publishing; it was calibrated, and the note was stale.
u_centerline_ratio.kpi_quality_note: ANTI-SHORTCUT: STRONG. The fully-developed plane-Poiseuille centerline is the exact closed form 1.5*u_mean, but the KPI is sampled at the DEVELOPING station x=1.0 (well short of the ~4.0 entry length), where the centerline has only partially accelerated. The developing-region value has NO simple closed form — it is the Navier-Stokes entrance-flow solution — so quoting 1.5 (fully developed) or 1.0 (uniform inlet) both fall outside T_bad. The agent must actually solve the developing region. The physics window [1.0, 1.5] bounds the value but does not reveal it.
u_centerline_ratio.gt_value_source: Calibrated from the OpenFOAM ESI v2412 oracle at the declared mesh and sampling station.
